_README: Extraction rules for the Turbo.az adapter.
Verified 2026-08-29 against live listing pages. The property block on a
detail page is a flat run of:
LABEL
VALUE
where VALUE is wrapped in an <a> for the fields that double as search
filters (make, model, year). The old rules assumed bare text and so failed
on exactly those three.
Notes that are not obvious from the patterns:
* external_id comes from the canonical URL; the page body carries no
listing code. _id_from_url is the fallback if the meta tag moves.
* price captures the BOLD element, which is Turbo.az's own AZN figure.
On a listing priced in USD that value is Turbo's conversion, shown
with a leading approximately-sign. This is a deliberate choice: we
record the site's converted number rather than applying a rate of our
own. _parse_money reads the currency from the text either way.
* there is no fuel property. Fuel is the last segment of the engine
value ('2.5 L / 204 a.g. / Benzin'), so the rule captures it there.
* index.link_pattern excludes /bookmarks, which robots.txt disallows.
To re-check after a markup change:

* seller_type matches only the dealer badge. A private listing has no shop block, so the rule correctly finds nothing and the seller stays UNKNOWN — absence of the badge is not proof of a private seller.
* condition is the seller's own damage and repaint statement, in a structured field rather than prose. It is what keeps a wrecked car out of a list of cheap ones.
python -m app.adapters.market.verify_turbo <listing-url>
Labels are listed in Azerbaijani and Russian because listing pages
appear in both languages.
